mainTopic: When a miscarried fetus counts as a human birth: animal shapes, the human face, and defects
overview: The גמרא first tries to prove from a משנה in בכורות that an animal-shaped fetus born to a woman cannot survive. רבא rejects the proof, because firstborn status for inheritance follows its own פסוק, ראשית אונו: the בכור must be a child the father would mourn. Next, רב אדא בר אהבה asks אביי the reverse case according to רבי מאיר. If a human-shaped fetus is found inside a slaughtered animal, may it be eaten? A proof from רבי יוחנן's pigeon case is pushed aside, since a human foot is at least like a hoof. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's argument over how much human form a miscarried fetus needs for טומאת לידה. רב says the face decides. There are two versions of what רבי מאיר and חכמים hold, and רבי יוחנן (the whole face) and חסא (half the face) each follow one of them. אביי answers a ברייתא that seems to say one feature is enough. רבא then rules on a fetus with one eye or one thigh and on a sealed וושט. A ברייתא defines a גוף אטום, and the question of how much must be missing continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: A משנה about miscarriages and firstborn status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה to support the view that an animal-shaped fetus cannot survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned in a משנה: If a woman miscarries something shaped like a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird, it counts as a real offspring. That is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say it counts only if it has some human form. And if a woman miscarries a fish-shaped 'sandal', an afterbirth, a sac with tissue formed inside, or a fetus that comes out in pieces, the son born after it is a בכור for inheritance but not a בכור for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה (from בכורות) as evidence in the open question of whether an animal-shaped fetus can live. This step only lays out the משנה; the actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, an animal-shaped fetus counts as a real birth, so it 'opens the womb' and the next son needs no פדיון from a כהן. The משנה's list ends with a ruling: the son born after it is still a בכור for inheritance. That detail is what the proof will be built on.

keyTerms.meaning: A full-fledged offspring that counts as a real birth
An amniotic sac with tissue formed inside it
A firstborn for inheritance, who gets a double portion
A firstborn who must be redeemed from a כהן (פדיון הבן)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate kinds of בכור. A son can be a בכור for inheritance from his father and still not be a בכור for פדיון הבן, or the other way around.

phrases.english: We, too, have learned in a משנה:
A woman who miscarries something like a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird —

phrases.aramaic: וָלָד מְעַלְּיָא הוּא, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: it is a full-fledged offspring; these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the חכמים say:
Not unless it has some human form.
And a woman who miscarries a sandal-shaped fetus, or an afterbirth,
phrases.notes: A 'sandal' is a flat fetus that looks like a sandal-shaped fish.

phrases.english: or a sac with tissue formed inside, or a fetus that comes out in pieces —
the son that comes after it is a firstborn for inheritance,
but is not a firstborn for the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the earlier question of whether an animal-shaped fetus can live.
steps.raayaObject: That an animal-shaped fetus cannot survive
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בכורות about miscarriages and firstborn status

steps.title: Why the משנה shows the fetus cannot survive
steps.stepSummary: If such a fetus could live, the son after it would not be a בכור for inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you thought such a fetus can live, would the son who comes after it be a בכור for inheritance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the proof from the משנה. If the animal-shaped fetus could live, it would itself be the father's first child, so the next son could not be the firstborn for inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the next son as a full בכור for inheritance. That only makes sense if the earlier fetus does not count as a living first child. So the גמרא concludes that an animal-shaped fetus does not survive.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that it can live,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the animal-shaped fetus from the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא אַחֲרָיו בְּכוֹר לְנַחֲלָה מִי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: would the one who comes after it be a firstborn for inheritance?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quoted משנה proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: An animal-shaped fetus does not survive
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that the following son is a בכור לנחלה

steps.title: רבא rejects the proof using 'ראשית אונו'
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the fetus does live, but inheritance depends on a child the father would mourn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, it may live. But inheritance is different, because the פסוק says 'ראשית אונו', the first of his strength. This means a child whose death would grieve the father. It leaves out this one, whose death would not grieve him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the proof. The משנה's inheritance ruling does not tell us whether the fetus survives, because inheritance follows its own rule from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For inheritance, the בכור must be the father's first child whose loss he would mourn. A father would not grieve over an animal-shaped birth, so even if it lived, it would not take the בכור status away from the next son. That means the משנה fits both possibilities, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact (keeping the original possibility)
The first of his strength (the בכור)

steps.whatToRemember: Firstborn status for inheritance depends on 'ראשית אונו', a child the father would mourn. So an animal-shaped birth never blocks the next son from inheriting as בכור.

phrases.english: רבא said: Really, it can live,
but it is different there, because the verse says:
'The first of his strength' —
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17. The word אונו is read as if it comes from אונן, a mourner.

phrases.english: one over whom his heart grieves,

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאֵין לִבּוֹ דָּוֶה עָלָיו.
phrases.english: which excludes this one, over whom his heart does not grieve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא לעולם דחיי ושאני התם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inheritance ruling comes from a separate פסוק, so it does not show whether the fetus can live.

steps.title: The reverse case: a human-shaped fetus inside an animal
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks אביי how רבי מאיר would treat a human-shaped fetus inside an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה asked אביי: According to רבי מאיר, who says an animal-shaped fetus inside a woman is a real offspring, what about a human-shaped fetus inside an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It flips רבי מאיר's case around to ask what happens when an animal carries a human-shaped fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says shape does not decide whose offspring a fetus is, since what a woman gives birth to counts as her child. The question is whether that same logic means a human-shaped fetus in an animal still counts as the animal's offspring.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה מֵאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: רב אדא בר אהבה asked אביי:
According to רבי מאיר, who said

phrases.aramaic: בְּהֵמָה בִּמְעֵי אִשָּׁה וָלָד מְעַלְּיָא הוּא —
phrases.english: that an animal-shaped fetus in a woman's womb is a full-fledged offspring —
what about a human-shaped fetus in an animal's womb?

steps.triggerLanguage: בעא מיניה רב אדא בר אהבה מאביי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question built on רבי מאיר's view from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a human-shaped fetus inside an animal count as the animal's offspring according to רבי מאיר?

steps.title: What difference the question makes: eating it
steps.stepSummary: The practical issue is whether the fetus may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? Whether it is permitted to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain why the question matters in practice. The answer: it decides whether this fetus may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal fetus found inside a properly slaughtered animal may be eaten through its mother's שחיטה. If a human-shaped fetus counts as the animal's real offspring, it would be permitted the same way. If not, it would not be.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
For permitting it to be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical point of the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It decides whether the fetus is permitted to be eaten.

steps.title: Trying to answer from רבי יוחנן's pigeon case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests solving the question from רבי יוחנן, who said that a pigeon-shaped fetus found in a slaughtered animal is forbidden to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us answer the question from רבי יוחנן. He said: if someone slaughters an animal and finds inside it something shaped like a pigeon, it is forbidden to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רב אדא בר אהבה's question about eating a human-shaped fetus by pointing to a ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says a fetus shaped like a different creature, a pigeon, is not permitted by the mother's שחיטה. The proof assumes a human-shaped fetus is the same kind of case, so it should also be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Solve it, answer the open question
One who slaughters an animal according to הלכה

phrases.english: But let him solve it from that statement of Rabbi Yochanan,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who slaughters an animal
and found inside it the form of a pigeon —
it is forbidden to eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the question raised in steps 4-5.
steps.raayaObject: That a human-shaped fetus inside an animal is forbidden to eat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a pigeon-shaped fetus found in a slaughtered animal is forbidden.

steps.title: A pigeon has no hoof, but a human has something like one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: a pigeon has no hooves at all, but a human foot is at least like one solid hoof, so the cases are not the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, with a pigeon, there are no split hooves and not even a hoof. Here, with a human shape, even though there are no split hooves, there is at least a hoof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from רבי יוחנן and shows that the pigeon case is different from the human-shaped case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pigeon is totally unlike the animal it was found in, so it is forbidden. A human foot is like a single solid hoof, so a human-shaped fetus is somewhat closer to the mother animal. The question about eating it is left unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? These cases are not alike
A hoof, here meaning a single solid foot

phrases.english: How can you compare?
There, with the pigeon, there are no split hooves,
and there is not even a hoof;
here, with the human shape, granted there are no split hooves,
but there is at least a hoof.
phrases.notes: A human foot is one solid piece, so it is a little like a hoof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבי יוחנן; it does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pigeon has nothing in common with the mother animal, while a human foot is at least like a hoof, so the cases differ.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the pigeon fails, so the question about eating a human-shaped fetus inside an animal stays unanswered.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the human-shaped fetus is permitted. It only shows that the pigeon case cannot prove it is forbidden.

steps.title: רב: what everyone agrees about face and body
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה, רב says everyone agrees that a goat body with a human face counts as human, and a human body with a goat face counts as nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the חכמים say anything that does not have a human form is not counted. רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: Everyone agrees that if its body is a goat and its face is human, it is human. If its body is human and its face is a goat, it is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a woman who gives birth to a creature with an animal shape, and רב lays out the cases where רבי מאיר and חכמים agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב shows that the face is what decides. With a human face, even חכמים agree the mother is טמאה as after a birth. With an animal face, even רבי מאיר agrees it does not count as a birth.

keyTerms.meaning: It is nothing, it does not count

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: Anything that does not have, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: anything without a human form does not make the woman טמאה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
Everyone agrees:
if its body is a goat and its face is human, it is human;

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפוֹ אָדָם וּפָנָיו תַּיִישׁ — וְלֹא כְלוּם.
phrases.english: if its body is human and its face is a goat, it is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the eating question and starts a new discussion on the משנה's words of חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The face decides: a human face means human, an animal face means not human, and both רבי מאיר and חכמים agree on this.

steps.title: The real argument: a human face with one animal eye
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that רבי מאיר and חכמים only argue about a human face that has one eye like an animal's.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argue when its face is human but it was made with one eye like an animal. רבי מאיר says part of a human form is enough, and חכמים say it needs the whole human form.
steps.whatsHappening: רב finishes his statement by pinpointing the one case where רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, having some of a human face is enough to count as human. For חכמים, the face must be fully human, so one animal-like eye means it is not counted as a birth.

phrases.english: They argued only where its face is human,
but it was created with one eye like an animal.
For Rabbi Meir says: even part of a human form is enough,
and the Rabbis say: it needs the entire human form.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's statement from step 8, moving from where they agree to where they disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about a human face with one animal eye: רבי מאיר counts it as human, חכמים do not.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the face is what matters. Everyone agrees on a fully human face or an animal face; the argument is only about a human face with one animal-like eye.

steps.title: The רבנן cite a ברייתא with the opposite wording
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge רב ירמיה בר אבא: a ברייתא gives רבי מאיר the wording 'כל צורת' and חכמים the wording 'מצורת', which is the reverse of his version.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב ירמיה בר אבא: But a ברייתא teaches the opposite! רבי מאיר says 'any form', and חכמים say 'from the form'.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack the version of the מחלוקת that רב ירמיה בר אבא reported in רב's name. They quote a ברייתא that gives each opinion the other side's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ירמיה בר אבא had reported which wording belongs to רבי מאיר and which belongs to חכמים. This ברייתא swaps them. So the challenge is about who holds which view, and it does not question that there is a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Any (or all) form', one wording of how much human face is needed
'From the form', meaning part of the human face

phrases.english: (He said to him) [The Rabbis said to him]
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'he said to him'; the better wording, in square brackets, is 'the רבנן said to him.'

phrases.english: to Rav Yirmeya bar Abba:
But isn't the opposite taught in a baraita?
Rabbi Meir says: 'any form,'
and the Rabbis say: 'from the form'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the version of the מחלוקת that רב ירמיה בר אבא reported in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ירמיה בר אבא's report of which wording belongs to רבי מאיר and which to חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives the opposite pairing of wordings and opinions.

steps.title: If the ברייתא teaches it, then it teaches it
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא answers that if that is how the ברייתא reads, so be it. He has his own tradition, and they may follow theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If it is taught that way, it is taught that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה בר אבא does not argue with the ברייתא. He simply accepts that there is another tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not explain the ברייתא away. In effect he says: I received my version from רב, and if you have a ברייתא that says otherwise, follow it. This leaves two versions of the מחלוקת, and the next steps will use both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it is taught, it is taught': I accept that this source exists, but my tradition is different

phrases.english: He said to them:
If it is taught, it is taught.
phrases.notes: He is not giving in or arguing back. He is saying, 'Fine, that is your source; mine is different.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Acceptance of a different tradition, with no reconciliation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא would seem to prove that רב ירמיה בר אבא's version is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both versions stand as separate traditions.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the whole face must look human
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that the forehead, the eyebrows, the eyes, the cheeks and the chin must all look human together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says in the name of רבי יוחנן: the forehead, the eyebrows, the eyes, the cheeks and the chin all have to be human together.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement explains exactly which facial features count as a 'human face'. רבי יוחנן lists the full face, with both eyes and both cheeks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The features are listed in the plural (eyebrows, eyes, cheeks), so both sides of the face are included. The mother is impure only if all of these look human at once. This is a strict standard.

keyTerms.meaning: The chin, literally 'the heights of the beard'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
The forehead, and the eyebrows,
and the eyes, and the cheeks,
and the chin —
not until they are all human together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who holds which opinion to defining which features make up a 'human face'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole face (forehead, both eyebrows, both eyes, both cheeks and the chin) must be human for the mother to be impure.

steps.title: חסא: one side of the face is enough
steps.stepSummary: חסא lists the same features but in the singular: the forehead, one eyebrow, one eye, one cheek and the chin, all human together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says in the name of חסא: the forehead, an eyebrow, an eye, a cheek and the chin all have to be human together.
steps.whatsHappening: A second list of facial features is given. This list needs only one side of the face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forehead and chin are in the middle of the face, so they are always needed. For the paired features, חסא needs only one of each, which is half a face. He still requires all of these features to be human together.

phrases.english: Rava says that Ḥasa says:
The forehead, and an eyebrow,
and an eye, and a cheek,
and the chin —
not until they are all human together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more lenient list alongside רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One side of the face (forehead, one eyebrow, one eye, one cheek and the chin) is enough.

steps.title: The two lists match the two versions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן and חסא do not truly argue. One follows the version where חכמים say 'כל צורת', and the other follows the version where חכמים say 'מצורת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not disagree. This one follows the version that says 'all the form', and that one follows the version that says 'from the form'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the two lists differ. Each list is built on a different version of what חכמים said (the two versions from steps 10 and 11).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them follow חכמים. רבי יוחנן reads חכמים as saying 'כל צורת', meaning the whole face, so he needs both sides. חסא reads חכמים as saying 'מצורת', meaning part of the face, so he needs only half.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the one who says (following that version)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן and חסא argue about whether to follow רבי מאיר or חכמים. They both follow חכמים. They differ only on which version of חכמים' wording is correct.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the two traditions from steps 10 and 11 to a practical difference: a whole human face versus half of one.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this one is like the one who says 'all the form,'
phrases.notes: 'This one' is רבי יוחנן, who requires the whole face.

phrases.english: that one is like the one who says 'from the form.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the seeming disagreement between steps 12 and 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each opinion follows a different version of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן and חסא seem to disagree about the law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow חכמים, but each uses a different version of חכמים' wording.

steps.title: A ברייתא suggests even one feature is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says 'the form of a face' includes even one facial feature, except the ear. That suggests one human feature alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: 'The form of a face' that they spoke about means even one of the facial features, except the ear. Does that mean even one feature is enough?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge from a ברייתא. It seems to say that a single human facial feature is enough, which is more lenient than both רבי יוחנן and חסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even חסא needed half a face. This ברייתא says even one feature (other than the ear) is enough. So it seems to contradict even the most lenient list.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces what seems to follow from the source)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The 'form of a face' that they spoke of —
means even one of the facial features,
except for the ear.
Is that to say that even one feature is enough?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lists of features given in steps 12 to 14, especially חסא's half-face standard.
steps.kashyaTarget: חסא's (and רבי יוחנן's) requirement of many human features together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a single human facial feature, other than the ear, is enough.

steps.title: אביי's first answer: the ברייתא means every feature is required
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא is teaching that each facial feature (except the ear) is needed, and it follows the view of 'כל צורת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That ברייתא was taught to make each feature required. It follows the opinion that the whole face must look human.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from step 15. He says the ברייתא never meant that one feature is enough; it meant that every feature counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 read the ברייתא as 'even one human feature is enough.' אביי flips it: 'even one feature' means that if even one feature is missing (other than the ear), the fetus does not count as human. That fits the version where חכמים say 'כל צורת', meaning the entire face.

keyTerms.meaning: To be indispensable; without it, the דין does not apply
The entire form (of the face), meaning all features must be human

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'even one feature' as 'one is enough.' אביי says it means 'missing even one ruins it.'

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When that [ברייתא] was taught,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 15 that said 'even one facial feature, except the ear.'

phrases.english: it was taught to make [each feature] indispensable,
and it follows the one who says 'the entire form.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי תַּנְיָא הַהִיא לְעַכֵּב תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says one human feature alone is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means every feature (except the ear) is required, following 'כל צורת'.

steps.title: אביי's second answer: 'one' means one of each pair
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the ברייתא follows 'מצורת', and 'one' means one from each pair of features, like one eye and one eyebrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: really it follows the opinion of 'part of the form.' And what does 'one' mean? One of each.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second, alternative answer to the same challenge. He keeps 'one' but explains it as one of each paired feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ברייתא follows the version where חכמים say 'מצורת', meaning part of the face is enough. 'One' does not mean a single feature alone; it means one from each pair (one eye, one eyebrow, one cheek). This matches חסא's list from step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
Of the form; part of the face is enough

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers remove the challenge: either all features are needed (כל צורת), or one of each pair is needed (מצורת). Either way, one feature alone is never enough.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually it follows the one who says 'of the form,'
and what is 'one'? One of each.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר מִצּוּרַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to the same קשיא answered in step 16.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One' means one of each paired feature, following 'מצורת'.

steps.title: A fetus with one eye or one thigh: side versus middle
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if a single eye or thigh is in its normal side position, the mother is טמאה; if it is in the middle, she is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If a fetus was created with one eye or with one thigh, if it is on the side, its mother is impure; if it is in the middle, its mother is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling about a fetus born with only one eye or one thigh. It depends on where that eye or thigh is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the eye or thigh is on the side, where a person's normally is, the fetus still looks human and the mother has טומאת לידה. If it is in the center, that is not a human shape, so the mother stays טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: On the side (the normal human position)
In the middle (not a human position)

phrases.english: Rava said:
[If a fetus] was created with one eye or with one thigh,
if it is on the side, its mother is impure;
phrases.notes: On the side means where a person's eye or thigh normally sits.

phrases.english: if it is in the middle, its mother is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: נִבְרָא בְּעַיִן אַחַת וּבְיָרֵךְ אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the facial-feature debate to a new ruling on a fetus with a single eye or thigh.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single eye or thigh in its normal side position makes the fetus human (mother טמאה); in the middle it does not (mother טהורה).

steps.title: A fetus whose וושט is punctured versus sealed
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the fetus's וושט is punctured, the mother is טמאה; if it is sealed, she is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If its esophagus is punctured, its mother is impure. If its esophagus is sealed, its mother is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another ruling, this time about the fetus's וושט (food pipe).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A punctured וושט is a defect, but the fetus still counts as human, so the mother is טמאה. A sealed (closed-off) וושט means the fetus does not count as a human birth, so the mother is טהורה.
steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards that the hole is the 'better' case. But a punctured וושט is only damaged, while a sealed one is closed off, and here a sealed וושט means the fetus does not count.

phrases.english: Rava said:
[If] its esophagus is punctured, its mother is impure;
[if] its esophagus is sealed, its mother is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רבא about defects in a fetus.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Punctured וושט: mother טמאה. Sealed וושט: mother טהורה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: miscarrying a sealed body brings no טומאת לידה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a woman who miscarries a גוף אטום is not טמאה לידה, and asks what a גוף אטום is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A woman who miscarries a sealed body is not impure with the impurity of childbirth. And what is a sealed body?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that fits רבא's sealed-וושט ruling. The ברייתא then asks what a 'sealed body' means, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the sealed וושט, a 'sealed body' is not counted as a real birth, so there is no טומאת לידה. The question at the end gets the definition ready, which רבי gives next.

keyTerms.meaning: A sealed body; a fetus missing something essential
Impure with the טומאה of childbirth
And which is; what counts as

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A woman who miscarries a sealed body,
its mother is not impure with childbirth impurity.
And what is a sealed body?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on a related case (a sealed body), close to רבא's sealed וושט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Miscarrying a גוף אטום does not make the mother טמאה לידה.

steps.title: רבי defines a sealed body
steps.stepSummary: רבי says a גוף אטום is one missing a part that, if taken from a living person, would cause death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: It is one missing enough that if it were taken from a living person, he would die.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the ברייתא's question and gives the definition of a 'sealed body.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether the missing part is something a living person cannot survive without. If the fetus lacks such a part, it is a גוף אטום, and the mother is not טמאה לידה.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough that; to the extent that
That it would be taken away

steps.whatToRemember: A fetus counts for טומאת לידה only if it has a human form. A single eye in the middle, a sealed וושט, or a body missing a part needed for life all make it not count, so the mother is טהורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
[One missing a part] that, if taken from a living person, he would die.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּנָּטֵל מִן הַחַי וְיָמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question at the end of step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What counts as a גוף אטום?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A body missing a part whose removal from a living person would kill him.

steps.title: How much must be removed to cause death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how large a part must be removed from a living person for him to die, and introduces רבי זכאי as the one who answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much can be taken from a living person so that he would die? רבי זכאי says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question to pin down רבי's definition of a גוף אטום. It then names רבי זכאי, setting up his answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gave a general test: a part whose removal from a living person would kill him. That test is still vague, because we need to know how big the removed part has to be. This question asks for a clear measure, so we can tell when a miscarried body counts as a גוף אטום.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much: asking for a size or measure
Will be taken away or removed

phrases.english: And how much can be removed
from a living person so that he will die?
Rabbi Zakkai says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact measure behind רבי's definition of a גוף אטום in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How large a part removed from a living person would cause death, which sets the measure for a גוף אטום.
